title: Israeli Diplomat Offered Iowa Attorney General Free Trip, Then Asked for Favors

An Israeli diplomat offered Iowa Attorney General Brenna Bird a fully funded
trip to Israel weeks before asking her to invoke a state law defending Israel
against boycott attempts by the Turkish government, newly disclosed emails
from an Iowa Open Records Law request show. The 2024 emails also show that
Bird signed onto a statement denouncing the prosecution of Israeli officials
for war crimes by the International Criminal Court (ICC), along with a group
of other attorneys general, at the request of the Israeli government.

Bird lost a reelection bid earlier this month, and the emails do not indicate
whether she accepted the offer of the trip to Israel or opened the anti-
boycott investigation.

Bird's office did not respond to numerous requests for comment.

The emails, released in response to an Iowa Open Records Law request, provide
a window into how the Israeli government has increasingly leaned on U.S. state
governments for support--leveraging personal ties with officials to promote
laws prohibiting boycotts as well as other forms of opposition to Israeli
policy. Israeli officials have also mobilized state governments to intervene
in international forums where it has come under pressure over the genocide in
Gaza and ongoing wars across the Middle East.

The Israeli government's requests "would certainly raise [U.S. Foreign Agent
Registration Act] alarm bells if the individual complied with those requests,"
said Ben Freeman, director of the Democratizing Foreign Policy program at the
Quincy Institute for Responsible Statecraft. "In the context of the Attorney
General having been offered an all-expenses paid trip to that same foreign
country, those alarm bells might seem much louder to a FARA investigator."

## Spirit of the Law

In February 2024, Bird received a joint email from the Consulate General of
Israel to the Midwest, the National Association of Attorneys General, and an
organization called the America-Israel Friendship League offering her a "study
tour to Israel" along with other state attorneys general from May 25 to June 2
of that year. The offer was a generous one, including full "costs of NY-Tel
Aviv flights, all in-country transportation, hotel accommodations, touring and
entrance fees, most meals and insurance." (Treg Taylor, Alaska's attorney
general at the time, attended the trip and
[listed](https://www.adn.com/politics/2026/09/17/treg-taylor-
accepted-69000-in-travel-related-gifts-last-year/) its value as $7,200 on an
ethics disclosure.)

The email record does not indicate whether Bird accepted the trip, and Iowa
Ethics and Campaign Disclosure Board
[filings](https://webapp.iecdb.iowa.gov/publicReports/gb-reports) for 2024 do
not mention it.

A few weeks later, in April 2024, Consul General Yinam Cohen came back to
Bird's office asking for a favor. The previous month, Turkish President Recep
Tayyip Erdoğan had imposed a [trade
embargo](https://sanctionsnews.bakermckenzie.com/turkiye-imposes-a-total-
export-and-import-ban-against-israel/) on Israel after the opposition had
[attacked](https://thecritic.co.uk/issues/may-2024/the-king-and-the-boss/) him
for his family's business entanglements with Israel. Cohen wrote to Bird's
office with "instructions from Jerusalem," asking her to investigate whether
the Turkish sanctions violated the "spirit" of Iowa's [2022
law](https://www.timesofisrael.com/iowa-governor-signs-antisemitism-israel-
boycott-bills/) against boycotting Israel.

Iowa is one of more than 30 states with laws targeting the Boycott,
Divestment, and Sanctions (BDS) movement put into place following years of
lobbying by the Israeli government as well as federal pressure. Although the
statutes vary, they generally use public contracts and investments to penalize
companies that boycott Israel.[ Iowa's
law](https://www.legis.iowa.gov/docs/code/2023/12J.pdf), enacted in 2016 and
expanded in 2022, requires public funds to divest from listed foreign
companies and bars state entities from awarding them contracts worth $1,000 or
more. The laws have remained on the books despite scathing
[criticism](https://www.aclu.org/news/free-speech/laws-suppressing-boycotts-
israel-dont-prevent-discrimination-they-violate-civil) from civil liberties
organizations that have described them as a cynical use of antidiscrimination
legislation to restrict the First Amendment rights of American citizens.

In New Jersey, State Assemblyman Ravi Bhalla
[announced](https://www.politico.com/news/2026/11/14/new-jersey-brooklyn-food-
co-op-israel-01166241) in November that he will try to reverse a law passed in
2016 that bans the state pension from investing in any company that boycotts
Israel, which he called "antiquated and tone-deaf." If Bhalla succeeds, New
Jersey would be the first state to roll back Israeli antiboycott legislation.

Cohen personally attended the 2022 signing ceremony for the Iowa anti-BDS law,
[telling](https://www.jpost.com/bds-threat/article-702465) reporters that the
consulate had been "following" the legislation for months and was "moving from
one state to another to make sure that the anti-BDS legislation is being
implemented." The laws as written are designed to target commercial entities
rather than governments. But in his letter to Bird, he stated that "an inquiry
by the state of lowa would send a strong message to the Turkish government to
reconsider their decision."

Florida
[blacklisted](https://www.sbafla.com/media/mqodaonn/2026_06_09_-israel-
scrutinized-companies-list-for-web.pdf) both the government of Turkey and
individual Turkish companies in September 2025 under its own antiboycott laws.

The emails do not indicate whether Bird opened the investigation in Iowa.

In May 2024, after war-crimes prosecutors applied for arrest warrants against
Israeli and Hamas commanders at the International Criminal Court in The Hague,
Cohen contacted Bird again with another request. "I humbly ask that you speak
out against the prosecutor's decision to issue arrest warrants for members of
Israel's senior leadership which undermines the basic principles of justice
and due process," Cohen wrote to Bird.

A few weeks later, Bird [signed a
letter](https://www.myfloridalegal.com/sites/default/files/2024-06/2024-06-26-arkansas-
icc-act-letter.pdf) from 20 state attorneys urging the U.S. Congress to
sanction the ICC. The letter echoed many of Cohen's talking points, denouncing
the ICC's "equivalence" between Israel and Hamas. Two known attendees of the
attorney attorneys' study tour--Alaska's Treg Taylor, who came in fourth place
in the 2026 governor's race, and South Carolina's Alan Wilson, now the
governor-elect--also signed the letter.

Taylor and Wilson did not respond to requests for comment.

## Friendship League

Separately, an archive of hacked emails published by the whistleblower website
Distributed Denial of Secrets (DDOS) reveals the tight relationship between
the Israeli government and the American nonprofit offering the trip, the
America-Israel Friendship League. The league has organized over [150
delegations](https://aifl.org/get-involved/) to Israel, hosting Americans from
all walks of life, ranging from government leaders to school superintendents.
Although it is not registered as a foreign agent under U.S. law, emails
contained in the archive show the organization's leaders directly offering
their services to Israeli officials and asking for guidance and instructions
on their political activities inside the U.S.

The emails come from the inbox of Ron Prosor, the Israeli ambassador to
Germany and former ambassador to the UN. The correspondence between Prosor and
officials from the America-Israel Friendship League comes from a larger
archive of his correspondence obtained by Handala--a hacking group believed to
be linked to the Iranian government--and posted online by DDOS. A separate
hacked archive from the Israeli Ministry of Justice, obtained by Anonymous for
Justice and also posted by DDOS, shows more direct collaboration between the
league and Israeli officials.

The American-Israel Friendship league was collaborating directly with Israeli
officials, including on efforts to counter BDS, long before it organized the
trip for U.S. attorneys general, the emails show.

Press Agency, on March 2, 2026. Photo by Michael Kappeler/picture alliance via

In July 2014, the group's Chairman Kenneth Bialkin, who died in 2019, asked
Prosor for an advance copy of one of his U.N. speeches and asked him to edit a
league statement in November of that year. Three years later, in June 2017,
the league's Vice President Paul Kaplan met with Minister of Justice Ayelet
Shaked and Deputy Attorney General Roy Schondorf in Jerusalem.

"I wanted to follow up on our discussion about the government's efforts to
counter the anti-Israel and BDS activities. I would be pleased to join this
effort and contribute to its success," Kaplan
[wrote](https://search.libraryofleaks.org/entities/9793866.a03d93819a02b930bbfa3a12b0a7c9c26dbfab5e)
to Schondorf, who connected him to Ministry of Strategic Affairs Director-
General Sima Vaknin-Gil. Kaplan touted his activities "for many years in the
U.S. on behalf of Israel," including his role in the league.

Vaknin-Gil offered to set up a meeting. When Kaplan said he was back in New
York and asked how he could continue to help, Vaknin-Gil responded: "Not this
way paul. When we meet - gladly," she wrote back. "This is a whole strategy
and two years work plan. It is not something we can summarize in a few
sentences."

In the 2018 hidden-camera documentary "The Lobby," Vaknin-Gil was filmed
bragging to an American conference about her ministry's ability to leverage
clandestine intelligence and money. "The Israeli government can look at the
bigger picture and actually create this coordination and cooperation. We are
the only player inside the pro-Israeli network who can actually say that he's
filling the gaps," she said.

Freeman, the foreign policy expert, told Drop Site that FARA would apply if
someone "explicitly took actions as directed by Israel's anti-BDS campaign
organizers," but that the emails by themselves are not definitive.

The America-Israel Friendship League has never reported its activities under
FARA. Its executive director, Wayne Firestone,
[told](https://forward.com/israel/453286/us-pro-israel-groups-failed-to-
disclose-grants-from-israeli-government/) The Forward in 2020 that he did not
believe the league was required to do so.

Kaplan, the AIFL, and Israel's consulate-general for the Midwest did not
respond to requests for comment.

The organization, which is registered as a nonprofit charity based in New
York, received a [$150,000 grant](https://quincyinst.org/research/the-eighth-
front-inside-israels-1-billion-influence-campaign/#h-delegations-times-square-
ads-and-soft-power) from the Israeli foreign ministry in December 2025 for its
state-official tours. The organization also [took
$33,000](https://forward.com/israel/453286/us-pro-israel-groups-failed-to-
disclose-grants-from-israeli-government/) from Concert, a quasi-governmental
company set up by the Israeli Ministry of Strategic Affairs, recently renamed
[Voices of
Israel](https://www.theguardian.com/world/article/2024/jun/24/israel-fund-us-
university-protest-gaza-antisemitism).

Other emails from the Anonymous for Justice collection,
[reported](https://www.theguardian.com/world/article/2024/aug/17/israel-
foreign-agent-law-leaked-documents) by The Guardian in 2024, show that the
Ministry of Strategic Affairs wanted to funnel money from Concert to American
nonprofits in order to get around FARA requirements. Ministry legal adviser
Liat Glazer wrote in an email that "we will have means of supervision and
management" through "informal coordination mechanisms" such as "oral meetings
and updates."

## State Pressure

In its fight to legally stifle criticism of its actions and forms of
nonviolent political opposition like boycotts, Israel has increasingly treated
state governments in the U.S. as a primary focus of its lobbying efforts. Much
of this effort has focused on treating boycotts of Israel as a form of legal
discrimination and leveraging the lower stakes and lack of familiarity with
the conflict among local and state officials across the country.

"The Lobby's overall strategy to proscribe BDS rather than defend Israeli
policies was made in Jerusalem," wrote authors Ian Lustick and Eli Clifton in
the 2026 book "Israel's Lobby," noting how efforts had shifted from persuading
an increasingly skeptical American public to convincing pliable state
lawmakers to pass legislation favorable to Israeli interests. "State
legislators were generally ill-informed about the Middle East, naturally
sympathetic to those claiming to be combating antisemitism, and exquisitely
sensitive to imbalances in the messaging received on different sides of
obscure issues by mobilized constituents, lobbies, and donors."

A 2019 [strategy
memo](https://search.libraryofleaks.org/entities/10403249.69c6b14182752dca98297aa2bedd15d2dddb3802#page=9)
from the same Ministry of Justice archive suggests "leveraging" state-level
laws can combat boycotts and "promote a trend of messaging and momentum to
Israel's benefit."

In 2025, the Israeli Foreign Ministry sponsored 50 States One Israel, a
conference of American state legislators where Foreign Minister Gideon Saar
promoted antiboycott laws. That conference grew into the State Legislators
Israel Caucus (SLIC), a new nonprofit founded this year. As Drop Site
[reported](https://www.dropsitenews.com/p/israel-backed-nonprofit-lawmakers-
draft-legislation) earlier this year, SLIC's first meeting in Washington was
hosted at the Israeli embassy and funded by the Foreign Ministry.

Bird has continued her resolute advocacy for the Israeli government as Iowa
attorney general to the present day. Britain and the Netherlands have recently
imposed import restrictions on products from Israeli settlements in the
occupied West Bank. On November 9, the Washington Free Beacon published a[
letter](https://freebeacon.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/Final-
_UK_NED_Israel_Boycott_Letter__1_.pdf) led by Bird and signed by twelve other
Republican state attorneys general demanding that those countries drop their
sanctions.

"Your anti-Israel sanctions may thus disqualify companies from your nations
from contracting with our States, or require our States to divest from your
companies, which both deprives your citizens of potentially valuable economic
opportunities and deprives our States of potentially valuable goods and
services," the letter headlined by Bird warned, adding, "These unnecessary
economic harms derive entirely from your unilateral decision to impose
unlawful sanctions on Israel."
